q: What is feat-ed-limit-change-v1 in the early-delinquency project, and what happened to it?
a: It is a 90-day credit-limit change feature from cards.limits_history. Its +0.021 AUC on holdout-2024q4 was mostly leakage from limit cuts made after delinquency began. dec-ed-drop-limit-feature removed it; the residual gain was +0.002 (exp-204).

q: What came of exp-205 in the early-delinquency project?
a: Adding the payment-to-minimum ratio to the GBM lifted AUC to 0.803 on early-delinquency-holdout-2024q4 without the limit feature. That led to ed-gbm-v2 in September 2025.

q: What does ed-gbm-v3 in the early-delinquency project use as inputs?
a: ed-gbm-v3 uses feat-ed-util-trend-v1, feat-ed-cashadv-v1, feat-ed-minpay-v2 and feat-ed-bureau-slope-v1. feat-ed-limit-change-v1 is not used.

q: What is the current early-delinquency watchlist model for full-file accounts?
a: ed-gbm-v3, promoted to the watchlist on 2026-06-18, replacing ed-gbm-v2. Thin-file accounts remain on ed-logit-v1.

q: What AUC and score PSI does ed-gbm-v3 get on the early-delinquency-oot-2026h1 eval set?
a: AUC 0.809 against 0.796 for ed-gbm-v2, with score PSI 0.07 against the training population, on early-delinquency-oot-2026h1 (n=1,930,000).

q: Why did the early-delinquency project move the watchlist to ed-gbm-v2 instead of keeping the logit scorecard?
a: The GBM beat the scorecard by 0.039 AUC on early-delinquency-holdout-2024q4 (0.742 to 0.781). ed-gbm-v2 also beat v1 on Brier (0.058 against 0.061). dec-ed-gbm-for-watchlist adopted it for full-file accounts, with the scorecard kept as challenger and for thin files.
